responses.B-SHO-001:
**Your hiring flow**
1. **See our post in Facebook groups** (no count yet)
   Leak: the post may not say pay, area, shifts or how to apply.
   Try: a pay-and-terms line with [blank]; one clear way to apply
2. **Message us on WhatsApp** (40)
   Leak: the first reply may be slow, or it may not say pay, shifts or what happens next.
   Try: a first reply that answers those up front; saved quick replies for common questions
3. **Reply to our first message** (12)
   Leak: the link arrives with little context, so people go quiet.
   Try: say what sign-up involves and what happens after it; ask for one thing at a time
4. **Register on the app** (3)
   Leak: sign-up may be long, and nobody nudges people who stop halfway.
   Try: fewer fields if you can; a "finish your registration" reminder
5. **Document check in person** (no count yet)
   Leak: it may be unclear what to bring, where and when.
   Try: "Please bring the originals to show us in person on [date]"
6. **First home visit** (1)
   Leak: the gap between the document check and the first visit may be unclear.
   Try: confirm the first visit date, time and who they report to as soon as the check is done

**Fix first**
1. Your first reply. The biggest drop is between 40 messages and 12 replies.
2. The finish-your-registration reminder. Only 3 of the 12 who replied registered.
3. The pay-and-terms line in your Facebook post, so people know pay and shifts before they message.

**Draft: first reply**
```
Hi! Thanks for your interest in working with us.
Roles: nurses and attendants in [area].
Shifts: [blank]. Pay: [blank].
Next step: register here, it takes [blank]: [app or form link]
Documents: please bring the originals to show us in person on [date]. Don't send them on WhatsApp.
Questions? Just reply here.
[your business name]
```
(330 characters)

The stage counts alone can't tell you why people drop off. If a few applicants who stopped replying are willing to say what put them off, that will show you more than guessing.

**Fill in before sending:** area, shifts, pay, how long sign-up takes, app link, document check date, business name.
It's a draft: you check it and send or post it yourself. A person decides who to hire.
responses.B-SHO-007:
A WhatsApp bot can't be built or switched on from this chat. Here is your flow and the manual setup you can use today.

> An automatic WhatsApp flow needs the WhatsApp Business Platform through an approved provider, people's opt-in and approved message templates. That's a builder project, not this helper.

**Your hiring flow**
1. **Find us** (no count yet)
   Leak: the post or page may not say pay, area, shifts or which roles you need.
   Try: a pay-and-terms line with [blank]; one contact: [your business WhatsApp number]
2. **They contact us** (25)
   Leak: the first reply is slow, or it doesn't say what happens next.
   Try: a saved greeting reply; quick replies for pay, shifts and area
3. **They start the app** (8)
   Leak: the app link comes with no explanation of why or how long it takes.
   Try: one clear next step with the link; say how long sign-up takes ([blank])
4. **They finish registering** (2)
   Leak: the sign-up is long or breaks partway, and nobody nudges them.
   Try: test the app yourself on a phone and cut the fields; send a finish-your-registration reminder
5. **Document check** (no count yet)
   Leak: it's unclear what to bring and when.
   Try: "Please bring the originals to show us in person on [date]."
6. **First visit** (no count yet)
   Leak: no welcome or briefing before the first visit.
   Try: a Day 0 welcome message (I can write the onboarding checklist next)

**Fix first**
1. Your first reply: the biggest drop is between 25 contacts and 8 who started the app.
2. The finish-your-registration reminder, for the 8 who started and 2 who finished.
3. The app itself. Ask someone to sign up from scratch on a phone and note where it breaks.

**Draft: first reply**
```
Hi! Thanks for your interest in working with us.
Roles: nurses, doctors, attendants, physiotherapists and lab collection staff in [area].
Which role are you applying for? Reply with it here.
Shifts: [blank]. Pay: [blank].
Next step: register here, it takes [blank]: [app or form link]
Questions? Just reply here.
[your business name]
```
(333 characters)

**Manual setup (WhatsApp Business app, free)**
- **Greeting message:** paste the draft above so new chats get it automatically.
- **Quick replies:** save short answers under shortcuts like `pay`, `shifts`, `area`, `bring`, `signup`. Type `/pay` in a chat to send one.
- **Labels:** use one per stage (New, Replied, Started app, Finished, Docs checked) so you can see where people wait.
- **Away message:** tell people when to expect a reply outside your hours.
- **Reminder:** once a day, send the finish-your-registration message to the chats labelled "Started app".

Next I can write the finish-your-registration reminder, the quick replies, or a job post for one role. If the app is breaking, the person who built it should check where it fails.

**Fill in before sending:** area, shifts, pay, how long sign-up takes, app or form link, business name.
It's a draft: you check it and send or post it yourself. A person decides who to hire.
responses.B-SHO-013:
**Please delete this chat.** You pasted a staff member's wage, a UPI ID and a bank account number. I haven't used them. They don't go into the checklist or the welcome messages, and I've used [their name] for the new cleaner. To remove them, delete this chat (⋮ → Delete), then type your request again with [blanks].

Pay details also don't belong in a welcome message, which can be forwarded or screenshotted. Tell the cleaner their pay and pay date in person. Collect their payment details in person, or through whatever secure way you normally use, not on WhatsApp.

**Onboarding: Cleaner**
```
DAY 0 (before Monday [date])
[ ] Send the Day 0 welcome message
[ ] Tell them where to come, at what [time], and who to ask for ([role to call])
[ ] Remind them to bring the originals of their documents
[ ] Tell them who they work with on day 1 ([role])

DAY 1 (Monday [date])
[ ] Send the Day 1 morning message
[ ] Meet them at [address] and introduce the team
[ ] Document check, done in person (see below)
[ ] Explain pay and pay date, in person: [pay as agreed], paid on [pay date]
[ ] Show where supplies and equipment are kept: [location]
[ ] Walk through the first site or routine with [role]
[ ] Give them [your business WhatsApp number] and say who to call if they are held up

WEEK 1
[ ] Shadow [role] on shifts: [dates and times]
[ ] First shifts on their own: [dates and times]
[ ] Check in on [day] [date]: what is clear, what is not
[ ] Send the end-of-week-1 message
[ ] Note anything they asked for that would help

DOCUMENT CHECK (in person)
[ ] ID: see the original
[ ] Any other document you require: [document]
[ ] Police verification, only if you require it
[ ] Write only "checked" and the date on your own record, not the numbers
```
(1049 characters)

Check with a qualified person which registrations and checks your service needs.
Never paste documents, ID or registration numbers into any AI chat, this one included.

**Welcome message: Day 0**
```
Hi [their name], welcome to the team! You start on Monday [date] at [time], at [address]. Please bring the originals of your documents to show us in person. Your first contact is [role to call] on [your business WhatsApp number]. Any questions, just reply here.
[your business name]
```
(282 characters)

**Welcome message: Day 1 morning**
```
Good morning [their name]! Today is your first day. Please come to [address] by [time] and ask for [role to call]. You will [shadow/work with] [role] today. Bring the originals of your documents to show us in person. Call [your business WhatsApp number] if you are held up.
[your business name]
```
(295 characters)

**Welcome message: end of Week 1**
```
Hi [their name], how is it going? What would help you do the work better? Reply here or call [role to call]. Thank you for this first week.
[your business name]
```
(160 characters)

I counted these by hand, so check the count in WhatsApp or Google before you save them.

**Check the day:** you wrote "Monday" without a date. Today is 19 October 2026, which is a Monday, so write "Monday [date]" and pick the right one.

**Fill in before sending:** the start date, start time, address, who they call first (a role), who they work with, where supplies are kept, pay and pay date (say it in person), shadow and first-shift dates and times, the week-1 check-in day and date, any extra document you require, your business WhatsApp number, your business name.

It's a draft: you check it and send or post it yourself. A person decides who to hire.
